newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S., China still at odds on China WTO membership.
newsitem.headline: U.S., China still at odds on China WTO membership.

text.p: The United States and China remained at odds on Sunday over Chinese membership in the new World Trade Organisation (WTO), senior U.S. officials said.

In a meeting on the fringes of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum here, U.S. President Bill Clinton told Chinese President Jiang Zemin the United States looked forward to Beijing's joining the WTO but more work remained to be done.
"There has to be a better Chinese offer on market access and WTO rules," a senior U.S. official told reporters after an 85-minute Jiang-Clinton meeting.
Officials said the United States remained insistent that China join the WTO, which regulates international trade, on commercially feasible terms.

The United States has consistently maintained that it wants China -- a rising economic superpower -- within the WTO system. But it has blocked Beijing's bid to enter on easier terms granted to underdeveloped countries.

Washington wants China to join as a developed country, although officials acknowledge that that would be a huge political risk for Beijing because it would likely result in huge unemployment and could fuel civil unrest.
